clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old male sustained a crush injury to the foot during a motorcycle accident with no fracture evident on initial X-ray. Vascular supply and nerve function remained intact. MRI performed shortly after injury revealed two serous fluid collections (~48 cc subcutaneous and ~38 cc superficial fascial) causing plantar swelling, with extension near the phalanges and an underlying stress fracture. These imaging findings supported the diagnosis of a closed degloving injury (Morel-Lavallée lesion). The patient underwent incision, drainage, and tissue debridement of the serous collections with serial aseptic dressings, resulting in dermal regeneration and discharge.
